one_month_reasoning: The window contains Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-28 (before the open, call 1pm ET) [14]. Guidance is $9.3-9.4B sales and $1.40-1.42 pre-split adj EPS ($0.70-0.71 post-split); consensus already sits above the top of the range at $0.722 [3][1]. Amphenol has beaten the high end of its guidance for many quarters running, so a beat is the expected outcome and mostly priced in. What moves the stock is the Q4 guide and the book-to-bill (1.23 in Q2) [1]. The 2026 reactions went both ways: after Q1 the stock fell about 19% in a month on a Q2 guide below consensus [9], and after Q2 it rallied. The bear-side risks for this print: comms networks are guided down mid-teens [2], the market is rotating away from AI hardware as 2027 capex growth slows [8], and the stock is up from $77.65 on Sep 15 to $85.67, close to its $89.26 high. The bull side: CommScope accretion keeps getting raised and IT datacom grew 63% organically [2]. Net, I see no edge on direction. I centre the distribution at about $85.9, roughly flat, with sigma of about 13.5% for the month. That is the stock's usual 46%/3.5 = 13%, widened a little for the earnings event.

fair_value.method: Blend of 60% forward P/E and 40% FCF yield, both at the 2027-10-01 horizon. P/E: skeptic-adjusted NTM EPS of $3.45 x 24x = $82.8. FCF: NTM FCF/share of $2.90 / 3.5% = $82.9. Blended about $83, slightly below the $85.67 price. The business is excellent but the price already assumes it.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 (roughly Q4'27-Q3'28) of $3.45 x 24x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus of $3.28 trimmed about 4%. The cut reflects UBS's forecast that hyperscaler capex growth slows from 76% to 25% in 2027 [8], comms networks guided down mid-teens [2], and estimates that jumped about 15% in 90 days [3], which leaves room for disappointment.
$3.15 grown about 10%. That is half of consensus 2027 growth (23%) because UBS sees 2028 capex growth at just 6% [8].
Pre-split figures divided by 2 for the 2-for-1 split effective 2026-09-03.

Today's forward P/E is about 25-26x [5]. The median AI-infrastructure forward P/E has de-rated from 32x to 22x [8]. A skeptic newsletter puts intrinsic value well below the current multiple [5]. I use 24x: a premium to the 22x AI-infrastructure median for APH's diversification and execution, but below today's level as growth normalises from 30%+ organic.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF/share of $2.90 at horizon, valued at a 3.5% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Pre-split diluted count doubled for the 2-for-1 split.

Q2 FCF of $1.2B on EPS of $0.675 means conversion of roughly 70% of net income, depressed by the working-capital build. I assume conversion recovers to about 85% of NTM net income ($3.45 x 2,578M = $8.9B).

The skeptic newsletter puts the trailing FCF yield at 1.42% [5]. I assume the yield normalises to 3.5% once growth slows toward the high teens. That is still a premium multiple: an A3/A- credit [6] with high returns on capital.
Shown as a check on leverage. FCF here is levered, so net debt is not subtracted again.

bear.story: In 2027 hyperscaler capex growth slows sharply (UBS: +25% in 2027, +6% in 2028) and AI orders normalise after customers double-ordered. Book-to-bill falls below 1. Comms networks keep shrinking. FY2027 EPS comes in around $2.90 instead of $3.28. The multiple de-rates to about 18-19x NTM EPS of $3.0, in line with how the AI-infrastructure median already fell from 32x to 22x. Result: about $56, near the 52-week low of $59 and in the same zone as the skeptic newsletter's $54 intrinsic value.

base.story: Growth slows from 30%+ organic to the mid-to-high teens. CommScope is accretive as guided. FY2027 EPS is about $3.15-3.25 and NTM EPS about $3.50. The multiple compresses to about 24-25x, which offsets most of the earnings growth. The stock ends roughly flat, around $86. A great business delivering mediocre returns from a rich starting price.

bull.story: AI capex keeps running near Goldman's +54% for 2027. Rubin and copper-to-optical transitions add content, as Evercore argues (+20-40%) and as CPO delays to 2029 imply. EPS beats keep coming, with FY2027 around $3.60 and NTM EPS about $4.0. The multiple holds at about 28x. Result: about $112.

thesis_break_reason: A close below about $62 (roughly 28% under today, back near the May 2026 post-guide low of $59-61 post-split) would imply about 18x on consensus 2027 EPS. At that point the market would be pricing a real earnings cut, not just multiple normalisation. The likely causes are a falling book-to-bill or a lower guide driven by AI order digestion, or a hyperscaler capex cut. At that level my base case (EPS of about $3.2 growing low double digits) would most likely be wrong, not just a victim of the stock's 46% volatility.

key_uncertainties: Whether hyperscaler capex growth slows to about 25% in 2027 (UBS) or stays near 54% (Goldman). IT datacom is 43% of sales and AI drives nearly all of its sequential growth.
Multiple compression as organic growth falls from 30%+ toward the teens. At 26x 2027 EPS, about two-thirds of APH's value is tied to growth beyond current earnings.
Content per rack in Nvidia Rubin and later generations: 'cableless' midplane and CPO versus more connectors and backplanes.
Double ordering or inventory build at customers. Receivables rose from $4.7B to $6.8B and inventory from $3.4B to $4.6B in H1 2026 (partly the CommScope acquisition). DSO edged up to about 70 days.

Insider selling: the CEO sold about 686k pre-split shares at about $161.6 on 2026-07-31 (about $111M, option exercises), and the CFO, GC and HR heads also sold in early August. This is routine option monetisation, but none of the insiders were buying.
reasoning: Facts: Q2 2026 sales were $8.8B (+55% reported, +30% organic), adj EPS $1.35 pre-split, book-to-bill 1.23. The Q3 guide is $0.70-0.71 post-split EPS [1]. The 2-for-1 split took effect 2026-09-03 [11]. Post-split consensus EPS is $2.67 for 2026 and $3.28 for 2027, the latter up about 15% in 90 days [3]. At $85.67 the stock trades at 26x 2027 and 32x 2026 EPS. Market cap is about $221B and net debt $14.1B [1]. Skeptic lane: (a) Credit is not the problem. The May 2026 euro notes priced at mid-swap +50/+85bp with A3 stable / A- positive ratings, and commercial paper was zero at June 30 [6][7]. Net leverage is about 1.6x. (b) I found no accounting red flags or meaningful litigation in the 10-Q extract. The working-capital build is notable but mostly explained by the acquisition and 30% organic growth [7]. (c) Insider selling after the Q2 rally was heavy and one-sided: the CEO sold about $111M and other EVPs also sold [4]. That is a mild negative signal. (d) The real bear case is valuation plus the cycle. An independent newsletter (Sep 23) values APH at $54 and says about 97% of the price depends on future growth [5]. UBS sees hyperscaler capex growth falling from 76% to 25% in 2027 and 6% in 2028, and semis are the most crowded trade [8]. Hyperscaler free cash flow is turning negative [15]. AI-infrastructure multiples have already de-rated from 32x to 22x [8]. The Rubin 'cableless' redesign removes NVLink cable cartridges [12], though SemiAnalysis says CPO slips to 2029 and Rubin stays copper [13], and the BofA downgrade precedent shows how architecture changes hit the multiple [10]. The Q1 2026 guide miss caused a 19% one-month drawdown [9], which shows how fragile the multiple is. (e) Weighing it honestly: execution is exceptional, CommScope accretion has doubled to $0.30, and IT datacom grew 63% organically [2]. Consensus earnings will probably be roughly met. The issue is what the market pays for them as growth decelerates. My fair value is about $83 (P/E 24x on NTM EPS of $3.45, cross-checked with a 3.5% FCF yield). Scenarios are $56/$86/$112 at 25/50/25, for a mean of about $85 and a median of about $85, so roughly flat with a fat left tail. The distribution is a mixture of three lognormals around the scenarios. Its implied volatility is about 38-40%, a bit below the 46% realized, because realized vol was inflated by the split-adjusted Q1-to-Q2 whipsaw. I add some tail mass at both ends so 1-year moves of ±40% stay plausible given that 46% realized. Research limits: Seeking Alpha, the EBC article and macrotrends returned 403.
